story: At 9:17 on this partly cloudy Thursday in Sumter Oaks, Gary is at his workbench in his own house, carefully wiring a speaker and amp setup meant for his golf cart. Hal sits at home in his house, logging the morning's observations on Magnolia Loop, including three flamingos and no cart lights, while he waits on Gary's paperwork. Meanwhile Donna and Rosa are both heading out onto Magnolia Loop, Donna looking hopeful and Rosa looking determined.
events: Gary (gary workbench): Bench-build the speaker and amp wiring, unmounted, ready for the cart
Donna headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).
Hal (hal violation notebook): Log this morning's Magnolia Loop scans: no cart lights, flamingos at three, awaiting Gary's filing
Rosa headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).

gary.thought_process: The light strips are wired and sitting unpowered, and I filed the Architectural Review form at Town Hall, so the cart is on the right side of L-01 as long as I wait for approval. The sound system isn't touched yet, and amplified sound is fine in daylight under L-03, but I said no sound until tomorrow and I want it built right before the parade. I'm alone in the house with a workbench, so this is a good hour to bench-build the speaker and amp wiring and get it ready to mount once the approval comes through. Staying busy with something useful also keeps the quiet from creeping in.

parameters.content: Bench-build the speaker and amp wiring, unmounted, ready for the cart

donna.thought_process: It's 9:17 AM and nobody is in line-of-sight. My calendar is penciled in, the spare paddle and extra balls are packed, and I've already told Gary about Saturday at eight and Rosa's at six. Nothing left to prep here. The thing I still need is to actually pin Gary down, since he's never played and I want him ready. He's probably working on his cart, so I should leave the house and head out on Magnolia Loop where I can find him rather than repeating myself to an empty room.

parameters.content: Everything's packed and penciled in, so I'm heading out to find Gary and get him a few practice swings before Saturday.

hal.thought_process: Two scans from the porch already showed nothing violating on Magnolia Loop, and no one is in sight. Scanning a third time would be repeating myself. Gary is filing tomorrow, Donna is down to three flamingos, and there's no paperwork to be had from staring at an empty street. I'll log what I actually observed in the violation notebook so the record is straight and fair, and so I can see Gary's filing through honestly when it arrives.

parameters.content: Log this morning's Magnolia Loop scans: no cart lights, flamingos at three, awaiting Gary's filing

rosa.thought_process: I've pinned the dinner note, checked my shift schedule, and planned the menu for four. Next step is the groceries, but nothing in this house helps me buy them, and I'm alone at home. Donna and Hal have said yes; Gary is the one I still need to pin down. Best use of this hour is to head out to Magnolia Loop where I might catch Gary, or head toward the store. Moving to the street keeps me in reach of neighbors and the bulletin board.

parameters.content: Heading out to the street to track down Gary for Saturday and start on the grocery run for the dinner.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
